newsitem.title: UK: Bournemouth soccer club sale agreed in principle.
newsitem.headline: Bournemouth soccer club sale agreed in principle.

text.p: English second division soccer club Bournemouth moved one step closer to securing its future on Wednesday after receivers said the club's sale had been agreed in principle.

The agreement will allow AFC Bournemouth Trust -- a group of the ailing team's fans -- to take control if the Football League, tax authorities and creditors approve at a meeting in May, receiver Alan Lewis said in a statement.

Bournemouth went into receivership in January with debts of 4.5 million pounds ($7.4 million), around half of which is owed to Lloyds Bank Plc. The bank has given its blessing to the sale agreement, Lewis said.
About 250,000 pounds is due to the tax authorities, which last month adjourned their attempts to have the south coast club wound up to allow it to play out the rest of the current season.
Fans of the club have rallied round their team and raised over one million pounds in a bid to turn it into Britain's first community-owned club, an effort acknowledged by Lewis.

"Before the Trust's public meeting at the Winter Gardens the situation looked hopeless. But the momentum generated..., the strength of public and player support, together with the recent match results, has given everyone great encouragement," Lewis said in a statement.
Many of Britain's lower division clubs are facing a bleak future as more and more of the income from television deals and merchandising flows to the 20 teams in the elite premier league.
